title: Oral History Reconciliation Archive

stages.name: segmentAccounts
stages.algorithm: Segment interviews into attributable accounts while preserving surrounding context and the speaker’s expressions of uncertainty. Distinguish firsthand recollection, hearsay, later interpretation, and quoted speech rather than presenting them all as equivalent historical evidence.
stages.gate: Attribution and evidentiary character remain explicit.

stages.name: resolveReferences
stages.algorithm: Resolve names, places, and relationships using authorized contextual evidence, preserving aliases and uncertainty. Avoid merging people with similar names or assuming a pronoun’s referent when the interview context supports multiple interpretations.
stages.gate: Identity links are evidence-backed or remain provisional.

stages.name: reconcileEvents
stages.algorithm: Compare accounts of potentially shared events, aligning chronology and scope while preserving different perspectives. Distinguish factual contradiction from differences in emphasis or memory precision, and do not manufacture one authoritative narrative from majority agreement.
stages.gate: Conflicting recollections remain attributed and searchable.

stages.name: formFollowups
stages.algorithm: Generate neutral follow-up questions that could clarify identities, chronology, or context without leading speakers toward a preferred account. Respect consent and participation boundaries, and distinguish clarification from challenging a person’s memory as false.
stages.gate: Questions are nonleading, relevant, and within consent scope.

stages.name: publishArchive
stages.algorithm: Assemble an attributed narrative and search index that preserve disagreement and access restrictions. Apply consent to quotations, identities, and derived summaries, and maintain edition history when participants correct or withdraw material.
stages.gate: No restricted content leaks through summaries, search snippets, or merged narratives.

operational_details: A participant withdraws one anecdote: invalidate its quotations and derived summaries without deleting unrelated consented material.
Two speakers use different dates for one event: preserve both with context.
A nickname refers to several people: retain candidate identities.
A transcript correction changes attribution: re-evaluate dependent narratives.
A restricted interview supports a public summary: ensure the summary does not reveal protected details indirectly.

scenario.representative_episode: Interviewees remember the same event differently, use overlapping nicknames, and have different permissions for quotation and public attribution.
scenario.independent_truth: Hidden interview attribution, event relationships, consent scopes, and preserved conflicting recollections.
